title: On thermal Hall effect in boson systems
authors: Yu. V. Baramygina, D. N. Aristov
abstract: We theoretically discuss the thermal Hall effect (THE) in boson systems keeping in mind possible applications to magnetically ordered insulators with skyrmion lattice ground state. The magnon spectrum of such systems may undergo a topological transition upon the variation of magnetic field, and THE could be a tool to confirm this phenomenon. We rederive formulas, suitable for our purposes, and find expressions which have a different temperature dependence of THE as compared to previously reported results. Particularly, in presence of anomalous terms in magnon Hamiltonian the thermal Hall conductivity has a small but finite residual 1/T contribution. Such contribution may become sizable at very low temperatures and resembles Meissner effect in superconducting metals.
summary: This theoretical work investigates the thermal Hall effect in boson systems relevant to skyrmion crystal magnets. By rederiving the thermal Hall conductivity, the authors highlight a finite, temperature-dependent residual contribution at low temperatures. This provides a potential experimental diagnostic tool to confirm topological transitions in these magnetic materials.
main_problem: The paper theoretically discusses the thermal Hall effect (THE) in boson systems, aiming to apply these findings to magnetically ordered insulators exhibiting a skyrmion lattice ground state.
main_result: The authors rederive formulas for the thermal Hall conductivity, finding a residual 1/T contribution at low temperatures due to anomalous terms in the magnon Hamiltonian, which resembles the Meissner effect.
method: The analysis uses linear response theory applied to a perturbation in the magnon Hamiltonian, involving the calculation of matrix elements and the inclusion of zero-point fluctuations.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a boson system, specifically considering magnon excitations over the ground state of a Skyrmion Crystal (SkX). The physics is governed by a Bogoliubov-de Gennes type Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Thermal Hall conductivity tensor (kappa_mu nu), Berry curvature (Omega^n_mu nu), and the thermal Hall effect (THE).
important_parameters: Low temperatures (T -> 0), magnetic field variation, and the presence of anomalous terms in the magnon Hamiltonian.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the perturbation is adiabatically switched on and initially neglects finite width geometry and edge currents compared to previous works.
paper_structure: The paper systematically derives the thermal Hall conductivity using linear response theory, first establishing the general formula, then incorporating zero-point fluctuation corrections, and finally analyzing the low-temperature behavior and the role of anomalous terms.
why_interesting: The detailed analysis of topological effects (Berry curvature) and transport phenomena (THE) in magnetic insulators connects concepts from condensed matter theory to observable signatures in quantum materials.
